Dynatec Madagascar SA Unveils High-Purity Nickel Product for Global Markets

Dynatec Madagascar SA, a leading player in Madagascar’s Metals & Mining sector, announced the official launch of its new high-purity nickel product on Thursday. The product, aimed at both domestic and international markets, is expected to strengthen Madagascar’s position as a key supplier of critical minerals used in battery manufacturing and stainless steel production.

At a ceremony held at the company’s Ambatovy facility near Toamasina, CEO Rivo Rakotomalala described the launch as “an important milestone for Madagascar’s mining industry.” He stated, “Our high-purity nickel product meets rigorous international standards and is well positioned to meet growing global demand, particularly in the electric mobility and infrastructure sectors.”

Dynatec Madagascar SA reports that the new product boasts a nickel purity of 99.8%, a specification verified by laboratory testing conducted in partnership with the Malagasy Institute of Industrial Technology. The initial production capacity is set at 5,000 metric tons per year, with plans for further expansion as market demand evolves.

According to the Malagasy Mining Association, the launch is expected to create up to 200 new jobs in the region and generate additional export revenue for Madagascar. “This initiative demonstrates the sector’s commitment to advancing value-added processing in-country,” said association spokesperson Fanja Andrianarivo.

Industry analysts at Antananarivo-based consultancy Minera Insights say the move could help Madagascar diversify its export base and enhance its role in global supply chains. “With high-purity nickel in short supply worldwide, Dynatec Madagascar SA’s new product positions the country to attract new investment while supporting sustainable development,” said Minera Insights’ director, Jean-Claude Ranaivo.

Shares in Dynatec Madagascar SA were unchanged on the local bourse following the news.
